courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: I'm bringing Ionic serve back up because the next steps can be tested in the browser and there,
I first of all want to work on the styling. Now for that,
let me go to my location picker and I'll copy the styles I set up there and move them into my
image-picker.scss file
and yes as I mentioned, you could definitely refactor the shell around our picker logic,
so this container because I'll keep that picker style just as I set it up here for the location picker
and location image will also stay the way it is, I'll rename it from location image to just image
though because that is the name I'm using here in my image
picker template. So let's wait for this to reload here in the browser, yes that looks better and now
let's tackle this error next. Now regarding that error in the browser, I mentioned that you can a) of
course prevent a fallback but b) we can also install a package that makes this camera work here.
I want to start with the fallback though because that would be a valid strategy as well.
Now how could that work?
Well, we probably want to find out if we're running in a browser or on a platform where it's likely that
we'll not be able to use the camera and that we can find out on which platform we're running
with the platform service. So let's inject platform here,
platform is imported from @ionic/angular and with that injected in ngOnInit here, I first of all
when I get a feeling for when what is true. So let's check platform mobile when this is true and I will
therefore output mobile here so that we can see which result, which result of this check here refers
to which check property. I will check mobile, I will check hybrid,
I will also check iOS here and Android and I also want to check desktop and
with all these checks added in ngOnInit, let's wait for this to restart and
let's see what we get here
and we should get this as soon as this new offer page loads. And we see actually here, surprisingly mobile
is true
and that is why I wanted to show this to you.
You might have expected that mobile is false here in the browser
since this looks like a mobile view here
but I'm still on my normal MacOS browser but instead it is true because this emulator here suffices
to send a signal that we're running this in mobile mode,
that also means that we can't take this as a signal for whether we'll have a camera or not.
We see that hybrid is false here though, so that's interesting.
iOS is true because I'm running this on my iOS simulator here and therefore Android is false and desktop,
that's also interesting, it's also false here.
So hybrid seems to be an indicator for whether we're really running this on a native mobile device
or not.
If I don't preview this in mobile view and I now reload, we can also see that we might want to position
these pickers differently but that's not the main thing,
the interesting thing here is we see mobile is now false,
hybrid is still false, iOS and Android is false but desktop is now true.
So desktop is really just true if we're viewing this in a non-emulated mode which would probably be the
default for your visitors from your desktop devices but you can't rely on this,
that's my main thing I want to emphasize here.
So with that, we know how to read that,
now how this is look like on our emulators? And for that of course,
we want to run our app on Android and on iOS to get a feeling for that or I will actually just run
it on Android because the only difference will be that iOS check and you can rely on that being true
on an iOS device
but we want to see what happens to mobile and hybrid and so on when we run this on a real native mobile
device. Here it's starting up on Android,
and now let's go to offers and then a new offer page here and to see the console log output, you can go
to run here in Android Studio, this run tab and here you will see your log messages.
These are log messages I'm interested in and what we can see here is that
mobile is true and hybrid is also true here
and remember, that was false when we previewed this in mobile mode on a desktop device
and therefore we can use this as an indicator.
